subject: Evaluation & ramp plan — pricing, true-up mechanics, and close timeline
messages:
From: Ellie Barnes <ellie.barnes@finosys.com>

Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Draft evaluation plan + timing

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Attached is a draft evaluation plan our technical team sketched out (FinoSys_MAP_v1.docx). We have three things to lock down before procurement will issue an LOI: a concrete evaluation timeline with pass/fail milestones, a clear pricing approach for the evaluation (and subsequent ramp), and how you handle retroactive true-ups if our usage spikes during the pilot.

High level: we want a 6-week evaluation that proves latency and quality on two primary flows. If that goes well, procurement will look to commit to a phased ramp over 3–6 months with an initial committed level and step increases.

Can you confirm:
- whether embeddings and batch / index building during eval count toward billable usage,
- a suggested economic structure (pilot discount, commit tiers, expected true-up cadence), and
- a target close date for commercial/contract (we're aiming for mid‑August).

Appreciate any sample billing math you can share so procurement can model it.

Regards,
Ellie Barnes
VP Platform Engineering
FinoSys

Subject: Re: Draft evaluation plan + timing

Ellie —

Great to connect. I reviewed the MAP and sketched a practical commercial approach so procurement can model costs quickly. Attached: Redwood_SOW_draft_v2.pdf and a short pricing worksheet. Summary below.

1) Evaluation (6 weeks)
   - Pilot pricing: 50% off hosted inference unit price for up to 500k inference tokens and 25k embedding ops.
   - Deliverables / pass criteria: latency < 150 ms p50 for primary flow, quality thresholds on sample prompts (see MAP).

2) Post-eval ramp (phased commit)
   - Month 1–2: 25% of target commit at pilot price
   - Month 3–4: 50%
   - Month 5+: full committed capacity
   - Commit discount tiers (revenue-based): 5% at $X, 10% at $Y, 15% at $Z

3) True-up & price protection (initial proposal)
   - Quarterly true-up (bill vs committed for quarter); retroactive true-ups limited to the prior quarter only.
   - Price protection: locked pricing for 12 months from contract effective date for committed tiers.

4) Billing/usage definition (proposal)
   - Billable Usage = inference tokens generated + embedding operations (indexing & queries) executed against our hosted vector store. Test/synthetic traffic excluded by mutual test flags.

Next steps: if that structure looks OK, I'll loop in Legal (Neha) and my manager (Marissa) to finalize contract redlines and the SOW. Happy to run through a worked example for procurement this week.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Tom —

Good question. For the eval we propose:
- One-time indexing of historical data = counted as embedding ops but eligible for a 75% one-time indexing discount during the pilot (we expect this covers large initial index builds).
- Ongoing embedding queries = billable at the embedding unit price.
- Sample invoice: assume committed tokens 1,000,000 for quarter, actual tokens 1,300,000 (30% over). With quarterly true-up (no retro beyond prior quarter) and a committed discount at 10%, the overage is billed at list price for the delta (300k tokens). We'll send a worked spreadsheet in a follow-up.

I looped in Marissa and Neha to get legal/commercial guidance on limits/caps.

—Priyom
From: priyom_das@redwood.ai <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: FinoSys redline points — pricing & true-up mechanics

Team —

FinoSys is pushing for minimal financial risk during eval and wants any true-up to be reasonable for them. They may ask for a 12-month price protection and no retroactive billing beyond the quarter, plus an explicit carve-out for "indexing spike" during onboarding. Procurement will escalate if we insist on unlimited retro true-ups.

Proposed commercial position for us:
- Keep quarterly true-up, retro limited to prior quarter only.
- Cap any retroactive adjustment (for a given quarter) at 25% of committed spend for that quarter (we can negotiate this lower).
- Offer one-time indexing credit during eval (75% off) and exclude a mutually-agreed list of onboarding tests from billable usage.
- Price protection: 12 months from effective date; extend to 18 months only for multi-year committed deals.

Neha — any legal concerns with the cap or definitions? Marissa — are these economics acceptable from a quota/discount perspective? We want to keep the deal competitive but protect our unit economics.

Thanks,
Priyom
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2026 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: FinoSys redline points — pricing & true-up mechanics

Priyom / Marissa —

High level legal feedback on the commercial points:
1) True-up cadence: quarterly is fine. We should explicitly tie retrospective adjustments to the same calendar quarter to avoid disputes about billing periods.
2) Retro cap: propose a cap of 20% of committed spend for the quarter OR the amount representing actual overage, whichever is greater — this gives FinoSys a safety valve but preserves our ability to collect meaningful overages.
3) Indexing carve-out: allow one agreed "initial index build" credit (75% off) during onboarding. Define indexing as "first-time vectorization of existing customer-owned corpora between contract effective date and 30 days after go‑live."
4) Price protection: 12 months from contract effective date; for multi-year deals (>=24 months) extend to 18 months.
5) Definition of Billable Usage: define as "Model inference tokens generated by customer requests + embedding operations (indexing and queries) performed by Redwood on customer-owned data stored in Redwood-managed vector indices (test/synthetic excluded by mutually agreed flags)." Keep the definition narrow to avoid third-party storage edge cases.
6) Recommend adding a mutual audit clause for usage measurement disputes, with a 30-day remedy window and a binding arbitration step.

I'll prepare redlines to the commercial annex reflecting the cap and definition language; note that procurement may push for a lower cap (10%) so be prepared to trade elsewhere (longer commitment or larger up-front).

Neha
General Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Draft evaluation plan + timing — proposed compromise and next steps

Ellie / Tom —

Thanks for the clear requirements. To keep things moving toward your mid‑August target, here is a compact compromise Redwood can sign to today:

1) Evaluation pricing & indexing
   - Pilot: 50% off inference units up to 500k tokens and 25k embedding ops.
   - One-time initial index build = counted as embedding ops but eligible for a 75% indexing credit during eval.

2) True-up mechanics
   - Quarterly true-up, limited to the prior calendar quarter only.
   - Retro cap limited to the greater of (a) 20% of committed spend for that quarter or (b) the actual overage amount.

3) Price protection & commitments
   - Price protection: 12 months from effective date (18 months for >=24 month term).
   - Commit ramp proposal: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over a 4-month staged ramp following a successful eval.

4) Definitions/measurement
   - Billable Usage = inference tokens + embedding operations performed against Redwood-managed indices; onboarding tests to be excluded by mutual test flags.
   - Mutual audit clause for usage disputes with 30 days to reconcile.

If this is acceptable at high level, we'll circulate redlines on the commercial annex (Redlines_contract_v3.docx) with in-line language for the cap and measurement definitions and send a DocuSign package. Can we target signature by Aug 18 so implementation work can start the week of Aug 24?

I'll include a sample invoice worksheet showing a 30% overage scenario for procurement's modeling.

Best,
Priyom Das
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
